_what: The Collection Collection (collection-collection.html, love.css §48): a dark gallery of our people's collections, one cabinet per collection, each under a lamp of its own and no two lamps alike. Built by tools/make-collection.py, which refuses rather than guesses. Photographs arrive through tools/intake-collection.py, which strips them before they are anywhere near the repository.
_cabinets: A cabinet is one person's collection of one kind of thing, named the way they named it. `owner` is how they are named on the label; `said` is their own sentence about it when they gave one, never ours; `given` says how the collection reached this file, and RELAYED is written as relayed -- the Pebble Board's and Samefood Cafe's rule, so the difference is visible and correctable. `build` is the house's guess at the right piece of furniture for that kind of thing (swatches hang, plants stand, rocks lie in a drawer) and is the owner's to change. The order is the order they arrived in and is never sorted.
_lamps: Every cabinet has a lamp of its own and no two lamps are alike, which make-collection.py enforces. A lamp is lit only when there is something in the cabinet to light; an empty cabinet stands with its lamp off and its label at full strength, because a label you cannot read is not a quieter label, it is a broken one (The Outskirts' rule). `lamp` is null until the owner chooses one, and the drawing shows no lamp at all until then: what has not been chosen is not drawn. The lamps themselves are defined in make-collection.py's LAMPS, each with the reason it suits the thing it lights.
_describing: THIS ROOM DESCRIBES THINGS SO THAT PEOPLE DO NOT HAVE TO. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-23: 'I can't title and describe and caption every picture myself. That'll prevent me from ever submitting a photo.' Writing alt text for every photograph of every pen is labour, and a rule that everybody must do it themselves is a barrier to exactly the people this site is for. So the house writes the title, the alt and the caption, and says it did: `words` is 'claude' when Claude wrote them from the photograph and 'owner' when the owner did. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE POLAROID WALL ON PURPOSE: polaroids.html promises 'we will not describe you in our words', because a description of a person is theirs to write. A description of a pen is not a description of anybody. Anything that shows a person goes through data/polaroids.json and not here.
_rules_for_whoever_describes: Describe what is visible and nothing else. Colour, material, shape, finish, what it is standing on, what is beside it.

Do not identify a make, a model, an ink, a scent or a maker from memory. A name typed from what something looks like reads as a determination and is a guess -- the herbarium's refusal to guess at a binomial. If lettering is legible IN THE PHOTOGRAPH, transcribe it into `reads` and the words may then use it. If the owner names it, it goes in `named` with `named_by`.

Look at the whole frame before writing a word. Nobody in it (a person goes through the polaroid wall's consent record instead) and nothing that says where it was taken: no address, no post, no window with a view somebody could place. Set `nobody_in_it` and `nothing_says_where` to true only after looking. If either is false, do not publish; say so to whoever sent it.
No value, price, rarity or count, in any field. See the house rules.
A title is a few words. An alt is one or two sentences a screen reader can say in one breath. A caption is one line that is not the alt again.
_licence: The photographs are NOT under the site's CC BY-SA 4.0 licence and carry no onward licence at all, for the polaroid wall's reason: CC BY-SA cannot be revoked, so a photo published under it could not be taken back when its owner asked. They belong to whoever took them. See LICENSE.
_withdrawal: Withdrawal is deletion. Remove the item (or the whole cabinet), delete its file in collection/, and run tools/make-collection.py. The tool refuses a file with no entry and an entry with no file, so nothing is left half-honoured.

cabinets.said: I have an extensive pen and ink collection.
cabinets.given: in Ryan’s own brief for this room, 2026-09-23

items.title: Blue ink and a dark pen, boxed
items.alt: An open black presentation box lined with folded silver satin, holding a round blue glass bottle of ink whose label reads PILOT, BLUE, 70ml, and a capped dark brown fountain pen with gold trim.
items.caption: Still in the box it came in, satin and all.

items.title: Two sleeves, one of them tweed
items.alt: On a wooden table, a red and black fountain pen with gold bands lies on a plush burgundy sleeve, beside a pink and purple tweed case holding a copper-and-black striped pen and a marbled navy blue pen, both with gold clips.
items.caption: Tweed for two, velvet for one.

items.title: Black pen with an engraved band
items.alt: A glossy black fountain pen with a silver clip lies on a red plush sleeve whose tab reads RICKSHAW. Its satin silver band carries a small engraved drawing between two rows of tiny squares.
items.caption: A silver band with a picture on it, and a mug just out of the way.

items.title: A green case of green pens
items.alt: A dark green leather case lies unzipped, with pens held in its elastic loops: a clear turquoise pen full of sparkle with a band reading SAILOR, a purple and teal swirl that shimmers, and a green and cream pen like broken stone.
items.caption: Greens in a green case.

items.title: Tortoiseshell, marble and black
items.alt: A tan leather pen case, flap open over a handwritten journal. In it: a tortoiseshell cap on a pearly white body with an ornate silver band, a swirled brown, cream and orange pen whose band reads Kilk, and a glossy black pen with gold rings.
items.caption: A leather case, and the journal open underneath.

items.title: See-through pens on a winter card
items.alt: See-through fountain pens on a card painted with a reindeer, a bullfinch on a post, a hanging lantern and snowy pines: one perfectly clear with gold trim, one teal-green with gold trim, and one smoky grey with silver trim.
items.caption: Nothing about them is hidden, least of all the ink.

items.title: Pens across a journal spread
items.alt: An open journal with a print of a red torii gate in water on one page and notes in coloured inks on the other. On it: a black pen with a wavy silver cap, a slim brass pen, and an amber see-through pen reading PILOT.
items.caption: Behind them, a tea bag in a dish and three sand timers.

items.title: Resin pens in a leather holder
items.alt: A brown leather holder with stitched slots sits on a green notebook on a rumpled grey blanket. Two of its pens are cast half in turquoise or pearly white and half in glowing orange-gold; the third is black with a gold clip.
items.caption: Half sea, half sunset.

items.title: The whole table
items.alt: A wide view across a wooden table at night: clear acrylic shelves stacked with ink bottles and boxes, open bags packed with pens and markers, perfume bottles, rocks and sand timers, and in front a laptop covered in stickers, one reading STIMPUNKS.
items.caption: Where it all lives, more or less.

items.title: Black, red and brass
items.alt: Pens side by side on a dark grey wood-grain desk: a black hexagonal pen with gold ends and its tip out, a red faceted pen with thin gold pinstripes that reads YSTUDIO, and a faceted brass pen that reads Kaweco BRASS Sport Germany.
items.caption: Pens with corners.

items.title: Purple pen on a pink sleeve
items.alt: A matte purple pen with a glossy gunmetal cap and clip lies across a pink fabric pen sleeve printed with a lattice of six-pointed stars, with a black tab that reads RICKSHAW.
items.caption: Purple on pink on wood.

items.title: Gunmetal pen on a pink sleeve
items.alt: A brushed gunmetal pen with dark chrome bands, clip and ends lies across a pink fabric pen sleeve printed with six-pointed stars, its black tab reading RICKSHAW.
items.caption: Same sleeve, different pen.

items.title: A row of pens under a list
items.alt: Fountain pens in a row on a wooden desk, under an open notebook listing pens and inks in handwriting, each line in its own colour: brushed gunmetal, matte purple, a purple see-through demonstrator, glossy red, bright blue, translucent purple and matte black.
items.caption: Lined up under the list.

items.title: Pens on a cutting mat
items.alt: Pens on a black cutting mat ruled in white: a matte navy pen with a wire clip, a blue and clear see-through pen with rose-gold trim, a sage green pen with a pearly white body, and a faceted metal pen shifting green to bronze.
items.caption: Ruled lines for pens that do not need them.

items.title: Peacock, burl and gold
items.alt: Pens on a turquoise tabletop: a teal pen with gold peacock feathers on its cap, one patterned like blue and gold burl, an ornate green pen with an openwork gold cap, a slim dark grey metal pen, and a brass pen reading HONGDIAN M2.
items.caption: From very plain to very much not.

items.title: A swirl in a white-lined box
items.alt: An open black pen box lined in white holds a shimmering fountain pen swirled in deep purple, blue and teal, with a silver clip and the words Edison Pen Co. engraved on its barrel. Behind it, the maker's cards are splashed with rainbow paint.
items.caption: Straight out of the box, card still tucked in the lid.

items.title: Ink boxes, laid out
items.alt: Boxes of fountain pen ink in rows on a dark wooden table, each one painted: a crescent moon over a stage, cats with green and yellow eyes, a lion, a night sky, a reef, Greek heroes in helmets, and a flower meadow reading LADYBUG.
items.caption: Every box its own painting.

items.title: Red and black, in suede
items.alt: A close view of a glossy red and black fountain pen resting in a box lined with grey suede, with a gold band near one end cut with a black flower.
items.caption: Lying in its box like it has nowhere to be.

items.title: Two reds on a journal page
items.alt: On an open dotted journal lie a red and black pen with a gold band set with a black flower and a slim glossy dark red pen with a faceted gold ring. A green bookmark quotes Virginia Woolf: books are the mirrors of the soul.
items.caption: The page above them is about perfume, which is the next cabinet along.
reads: Books are the mirrors of the soul
